title: Hypertension fuels osteoarthritis through neuroendocrine signaling
title_zh: 高血压通过神经内分泌信号促进骨关节炎
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease, the progression of which is accelerated by systemic metabolic stress. Here, we identified a neuroendocrine pathway through which hypertension accelerates OA pathogenesis in joints predisposed by mechanical injury or aging. Nationwide cohort analyses and hypertensive mouse models demonstrated that elevated blood pressure exacerbates OA pathogenesis. OA-primed chondrocytes up-regulated arginine vasopressin (AVP) receptor 1A (AVPR1A), rendering them responsive to hypertension-associated circulating AVP. AVP-AVPR1A signaling enhanced catabolic signaling while suppressing anabolic regulators, thereby promoting cartilage catabolism. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of AVPR1A protected against hypertension-driven OA acceleration. Transcriptomic profiling and gene-silencing analyses identified NR4A3 as the principal downstream transcriptional mediator. Collectively, these findings establish the AVP-AVPR1A axis as a mechanistic link between systemic hypertensive stress and joint degeneration.
abstract_zh: 骨关节炎（OA）是一种退行性关节疾病，其进展受到全身代谢应激的加速。在本研究中，我们发现了一条神经内分泌通路，说明高血压通过该通路加速机械损伤或衰老导致易感关节的OA发病。全国队列分析和高血压小鼠模型表明，血压升高会加剧OA的病理进程。OA预先激活的软骨细胞上调了精氨酸加压素（AVP）受体1A（AVPR1A），使其对与高血压相关的循环AVP产生反应。AVP-AVPR1A信号增强了分解代谢信号，同时抑制了合成代谢调节因子，从而促进了软骨的分解。对AVPR1A进行基因敲除或药物抑制可保护关节免受高血压驱动的OA加速。转录组分析和基因沉默实验确定NR4A3为主要下游转录调节因子。综上所述，这些发现确立了AVP-AVPR1A轴作为全身高血压应激与关节退化之间的机制性联系。
